title: Weights ingest and qualification pipeline for open LLMs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement an end-to-end pipeline to intake, convert, validate, and publish performance profiles for new open-source LLM weights. This ticket covers the server-side ingestion API, automated format conversion (HF checkpoints -> optimized deployable artifacts), deterministic validation (sanity checks + functional tests), quantization compatibility checks, automated profiling across a matrix of seq lengths and batch sizes, generation of a model manifest/model-card, and publishing the performance profile to the model catalog with a pinned model version identifier. The goal is to make onboarding repeatable, auditable, and fast enough that a new model can appear in the catalog with verified performance within a single business day (target: 8h engineer + infra work).
acceptance_criteria: Weights intake API accepts uploads or remote URLs; validates checksum + license metadata before enqueuing conversion
Conversion step produces deployable artifact (gguf/safetensors + model metadata) and a canonical model-id:version string; artifacts stored in S3 under /models/{model-id}/{version}/
Validation suite passes: tokenizer round-trip, single-GPU forward pass on at least 3 prompt shapes, and deterministic output check (where applicable)
Quantization compatibility report generated for int8 and int4 paths, with estimated latency and quality delta; flags models that exceed configured quality regression threshold
Performance profile produced for seq lengths [128,512,2048], batch sizes [1,8,32] including p50/p95 latency, peak GPU memory, and throughput; profiles published to catalog and linked to model-card
Model version is pinned and can be referenced by 'model-id@version' for serving; rollout plan (canary + full) is autogenerated for Hosted API
Automated smoke tests and canary rollout succeed in staging; rollback policy documented
Audit log entries record all steps (intake, conversion, validation, profile publish) with actor and timestamps
tasks: Design API contract for weights intake (multipart/form-data + metadata JSON) - spec in Confluence
Implement weights-intake microservice with size/streaming support and license checks
Integrate conversion worker that runs HF -> gguf and builds tokenizer+config bundle
Add deterministic validation harness (tokenizer tests, forward pass, shape checks)
Hook quantization compatibility runner (hf-quantize wrapper) and quality estimator using eval prompts
Build performance profiler that spins up measurement job across hardware flavors and records p50/p95/throughput/mem
Model manifest and card generator; auto-populate fields (license, params, tokenizer, tokenizer-fallback used, tags)
Publish step: upload artifacts, write model catalog entry, and emit message to console/catalog services
Create canary rollout template and staging smoke test suite
Add observability: metrics (ingest_latency, conversion_duration, validation_failures), traces, and dashboard
Write runbook for manual intervention and rollback
Add unit/integration tests and CI pipeline entry; create GitHub PR and link

notes: Trade-offs discussed: full deterministic output checks are impossible for non-deterministic models; we will instead enforce statistical regression checks on a standard eval set. For extremely large weights we will support remote-source ingestion (S3/HF URL) to avoid double-storage. Keep conversion idempotent and record the conversion toolchain version in the manifest.
